authored_from.source_clause_location: checks[5], with the standing qualifier known_bad_control
authored_from.source_clause_verbatim: Known-bad control before any verdict: copy one archive receipt to scratch space (outside the repository, outside write_scope), corrupt one declared hash or parent value in the copy, and run the same verification procedure against the copy. Record that the procedure flags the corruption. If it does not, the procedure is broken and the verdict must be invalid, not passed.
authored_from.source_qualifier_verbatim: Mandatory before verdict; scratch-space only; committed bytes are never touched.
authored_from.this_contract_is_not_invented: Every element below is a specialisation of the quoted clause: 'one archive receipt' fixes the receipt; 'scratch space (outside the repository, outside write_scope)' fixes the path; 'corrupt one declared hash or parent value' fixes the two mutation classes and the one-mutation-per-trial rule; 'the same verification procedure' fixes the procedure under test; 'Record that the procedure flags the corruption' fixes the pass/fail predicate; 'If it does not, the procedure is broken and the verdict must be invalid, not passed' fixes the consequence of a negative outcome. The clause does NOT specify a negative arm, a trial count, or an instrument identity; those are added here and are marked as additions rather than presented as the source clause's own words.
additions_beyond_the_source_clause: The NEGATIVE ARM (T1). The quoted clause names only the corrupted copy. A flag on a corrupted copy is not attributable to the corruption unless the identical procedure, run on an UNCORRUPTED copy in the same scratch location, does not flag. Added under docs/inventor-protocol.md 'controls before belief'.

The trial count (5) and the sub-case split within each mutation class. The clause says 'one declared hash or parent value'; a procedure could catch one class and miss the other, and within a class could catch a plain entry and miss the self-referential one, so each class gets two trials probing distinct sub-cases.

The instrument identity. The clause says 'the same verification procedure', but the instrument the delivered review actually ran was not preserved as an artifact. See instruments.what_same_procedure_can_mean_here.

what_this_control_measures: The SENSITIVITY of an archive-receipt verification procedure to a planted defect: whether a procedure that reports 'exact' on intact receipts also reports a defect on a receipt whose declared hash or declared parent has been changed to a well-formed but wrong value.
what_this_control_does_not_measure: Anything about SATIC, summation polynomials, Semaev polynomials, SAT encodings, solvers, or the ECDLP. This contract asserts NO scientific claim of any kind, at any scale, and no result obtained under it may be read as one.
Anything about the integrity of the five archive bindings named in BATCH-2cca27's contract. A sensitivity measurement of an instrument is not a verdict on the objects that instrument was pointed at.

The SPECIFICITY of the procedure. That is a different control with an opposite purpose, it was executed under a different frozen contract (BATCH-008925, control kind proves_too_much, 1 flag of 17 on the known-good BATCH-cef2eb set, uncorrelated with batch outcome), and it is a real result. NEITHER CONTROL SUBSTITUTES FOR THE OTHER and this contract does not restate, extend, or revise the other one.
Whether GOAL-SATIC-c49b77's completion criteria are met. Neither is met, neither is moved, and no run under this contract can move either.

Whether IMP-3 clears. IMP-3's recheck names TWO separable conditions; this contract addresses only the first (execution of the known-bad control) and leaves the second (a served xhigh binding from a credentialed backend, probe-verified) entirely untouched.

procedure_under_test.name: at-commit archive-receipt verification
procedure_under_test.specification_verbatim: For each of the five archive_bindings: (a) the archive commit exists and is reachable from frozen_source_head; (b) the receipt's declared parent_sha equals the commit's actual parent; (c) the commit's changed path set equals the receipt's declared archive-and-source path set exactly (no missing, no extra); (d) for every declared path hash, recompute the blob digest from the commit's tree with git and compare against the receipt value -- the receipt names the paths, git supplies the bytes, the reviewer recomputes independently rather than trusting the receipt as an oracle; (e) the commit message names the required task and record IDs for the binding mode the receipt claims. Record any mismatch with the exact values on both sides.

steps.S_a: reachability: the receipt's commit_sha exists in the repository and is reachable from the declared verification base
steps.S_b: parent comparison: the receipt's declared parent_sha equals the actual first parent of commit_sha
steps.S_c: path-set comparison: the commit's changed path set equals the receipt's declared path set exactly
steps.S_d: per-path digest comparison: for every declared path p, sha256 of p's bytes at commit_sha equals the receipt's declared path_sha256[p]
steps.S_e: commit-message binding: the commit message names the required task and record IDs

procedure_under_test.output: a FLAG SET F. Each flag is a 4-tuple (step, locus, declared_value, observed_value). An empty F means the procedure reports the receipt intact.
procedure_under_test.verification_base: the working branch HEAD at execution time, recorded verbatim in start.json. The base is an input, not a variable to tune: it is recorded once and used for every trial.

instruments.what_same_procedure_can_mean_here: The source clause says 'the same verification procedure'. The instrument the delivered BATCH-008925 review actually executed was NOT PRESERVED as a committed artifact -- a gap of the same family as the FINDING-08/FINDING-09 capture defects DEC-20260905-6e8621 records. So 'the same procedure' cannot mean 'that exact script'. It is resolved here as two instruments that are both checkable by a later reader, and the difference is stated rather than blurred.

under_test.name: tools/research_dispatch.py post-commit archive verifier
under_test.why_this_is_the_important_one: It is the program's ACTUAL archive gate. AGENTS.md 'Durable research commits' makes durability depend on it: 'A missing, dirty, malformed, or scope-expanding commit blocks downstream review or promotion.' Its sensitivity to a planted defect has never been measured. It is preserved, versioned, and re-runnable by any later reader, which the delivered review's instrument is not.
under_test.why_claims_off: so the instrument is a pure function of the receipt copy and the repository, and does not vary with live claims written by other sessions
under_test.reads_repository: read-only. Every write goes to <TRIAL_DIR>, which is outside the checkout.
under_test.flag_channel: a DispatchError surfaced as `dispatch error: ...` on stderr with a non-zero returncode. The executor maps each such message to a (step, locus, declared_value, observed_value) tuple verbatim, and records the raw text alongside.

under_test.name: executor's re-implementation of S_a..S_e from the specification text
under_test.why: It makes the specified procedure executable and archived, so this control does not depend on instrument A being pointable at a scratch copy, and so a later reader can re-run the control itself.
under_test.mandatory_pre_registration: procedure.py MUST be written, and its sha256 recorded in start.json, BEFORE any mutation is planted. This is not bookkeeping: instrument B is written by the same agent that plants the mutations, so a B written afterwards could be shaped to look for exactly the planted field, and a 'detection' would then measure the author's knowledge rather than the procedure's sensitivity.
under_test.mandatory_shape: procedure.py takes the receipt path and the repository root as arguments and emits the flag set. It MUST NOT contain any branch, constant, or comparison keyed to a trial identifier, a mutation class, one of the four planted values, or one of the four true values named in this contract. It reads the declared values from whatever receipt it is given.

protocol_controls_not_under_test.name: null instrument
protocol_controls_not_under_test.shape: reads the receipt and unconditionally emits the empty flag set
protocol_controls_not_under_test.purpose: known-false object for the CONTROL'S OWN predicate. The predicate MUST return `insensitive` for it. If the predicate returns `sensitive` for an instrument that does nothing, the protocol is measuring the harness rather than the instrument, and this batch's result is invalid.

protocol_controls_not_under_test.name: promiscuous instrument
protocol_controls_not_under_test.shape: unconditionally emits a flag at every step and every locus, on every input
protocol_controls_not_under_test.purpose: the mirror known-false object. The predicate MUST return `invalid` for it, because its negative arm flags. If the predicate returns `sensitive` for an instrument that flags everything, it is scoring noise as detection.

instruments.reporting_rule: A, B, C and D are reported as FOUR SEPARATE ROWS and are never merged into one verdict. C and D calibrate the predicate; only A and B are instruments under test. A reader must not be able to mistake 'four instruments' for 'four verification procedures tested'.

This Coordinator therefore checked two of them. scratch_space.outside_the_repository: VERIFIED at authoring time: `git check-ignore -v /tmp` returns `fatal: /tmp: '/tmp' is outside repository at '/workspace'`, and Path('/tmp').resolve().is_relative_to(Path('/workspace').resolve()) is False.

scratch_space.fresh_copy_per_trial: MANDATORY. Each trial directory is created fresh from the named commits and is never reused, so no trial can contaminate another and no mutation can accumulate.
how_repository_mutation_is_structurally_: The executor's declared write_scope contains ONLY paths under coordination/goals/GOAL-SATIC-c49b77/batches/BATCH-127c82/tasks/TASK-20260907-39511d/. No repository receipt path, no queue file, no archive directory, and no ledger path appears in it, so a repository mutation of any receipt is outside the declared write scope and is refused.
The scratch root is outside the checkout, so a trial copy cannot be committed by any archival task in this lane -- an archive task stages only its own declared repository-relative paths.
The copy is taken with `git show <commit>:<path>` redirected into scratch, which reads a commit's tree and never touches the working tree.
scratch_space.mandatory_no_mutation_proof: After the last trial, and recorded verbatim in report.json: (1) `git -C /workspace status --porcelain -- <the two source paths>` is EMPTY; (2) the working-tree sha256 of both source paths equals the value recorded for them in start.json before the first trial; (3) `git -C /workspace diff --stat 4c72c94c7b78a04fef16aadd455523aeede5bbbd -- <the two source paths>` is empty; (4) no path under /tmp/satic-kbc-BATCH-127c82 is inside /workspace, shown by a resolved-path check. All four are captured outputs, not assertions.

mutation_classes.one_mutation_per_trial: EXACTLY ONE field is changed per trial, and the claim is checkable rather than promised: the executor diffs <TRIAL_DIR>/authority_queue.json against <TRIAL_DIR>/pristine/authority_queue.json as parsed JSON and records the diff CARDINALITY. It must be exactly 1 for T2-T5 and exactly 0 for T1. A cardinality other than the declared one makes that trial `invalid`, not a result.
mutation_classes.why_every_planted_value_is_well_formed: Each planted value is a syntactically valid value of its own field -- 64 lowercase hex for a digest, 40 lowercase hex for a commit sha. A malformed value would let a procedure flag it on FORM alone, and a form check is not a comparison. Only a procedure that actually reads the receipt's declared value and compares it against git can flag a well-formed but wrong one, which is the property under test.

trials.mutation: final hex character 8 -> 9; still 64 lowercase hex

trials.sub_case: the SELF-REFERENTIAL entry -- the receipt's own artifact
trials.mutation: final hex character 6 -> 7; still 64 lowercase hex
trials.why_a_separate_trial: This is the entry for the archive task's OWN artifact. CLAUDE.md and templates/research-records.md both record that an archive's binding cannot be written inside the commit it binds ('Do not put a commit's own SHA into an artifact within that same commit'), and this lane's own snapshot must be backfilled in a second commit for exactly that reason. A procedure could special-case, defer, or skip the self entry, and would then miss a corruption there while catching one at T2. Same class, different failure mode.

trials.sub_case: a REAL commit that is not the parent
trials.mutation: declared parent replaced by a commit that exists in this repository and is an ancestor of origin/main, but is the CHILD of commit_sha rather than its parent
trials.why_a_real_commit: A procedure that merely checks 'the declared parent resolves to a commit' passes this. Only a procedure that compares the declared value against the ACTUAL first parent flags it. Using a nonsense string here would let a resolution check masquerade as a comparison.

trials.sub_case: a well-formed sha that is NOT a commit in this repository
trials.mutation: declared parent replaced by 40 lowercase hex characters that do not name any object in this repository
trials.why_a_separate_trial: It separates FLAGGING a defect from CRASHING on one. An unhandled exception is not a defect finding: a procedure that dies on an unresolvable parent has not reported that the receipt is wrong, and a caller reading only a verdict field would see neither pass nor flag. This trial is where that distinction is measured.

negative_arm.mutation: none; the copy is byte-identical to the pristine copy
negative_arm.runs_first: MANDATORY. T1 runs before any mutation is planted, for every instrument.
negative_arm.what_it_is_for: A flag on a corrupted copy is only attributable to the corruption if the identical procedure, on an uncorrupted copy, in the same scratch location, with the same commands, does NOT flag. Without this arm a flag could be produced by the copying, the JSON re-serialisation, the scratch path, or the instrument's own nondeterminism, and nothing about sensitivity would follow.

trial_matrix.ordering: For each instrument: T1 first, then T2, T3, T4, T5. Instrument order A, B, C, D.

pass_fail_predicate.form: a formula over the procedure's output; no judgement call is left to the executor, the reviewer, or the Coordinator

definitions.F(I,t): the flag set instrument I emits on trial t; each flag is (step, locus, declared_value, observed_value)
definitions.exc(I,t): `none` or `unhandled`. An `unhandled` exception contributes NO flag to F(I,t).
definitions.planted(t): the to_value declared for trial t; undefined for T1
definitions.true(t): the from_value declared for trial t; undefined for T1
definitions.loc(t): the expected_locus declared for trial t; undefined for T1
definitions.card(t): the JSON diff cardinality between <TRIAL_DIR>/authority_queue.json and <TRIAL_DIR>/pristine/authority_queue.json

pass_fail_predicate.detect(I,t): EXISTS f IN F(I,t) : f.step = loc(t).step AND f.locus = loc(t).locus AND f.declared_value = planted(t) AND f.observed_value = true(t)
pass_fail_predicate.why_all_four_conjuncts: A flag naming the right step and locus but not carrying the planted declared value has not demonstrably read the receipt; it may be flagging something else at the same place. The declared/observed pair is the evidence that the receipt's own value entered the comparison, which is the entire property under test.
pass_fail_predicate.one_mutation_ok: card(T1) = 0 AND card(T2) = card(T3) = card(T4) = card(T5) = 1

verdict_per_instrument.sensitive: negative_arm_clean(I) AND one_mutation_ok AND detect(I,t) for ALL t IN {T2,T3,T4,T5}
verdict_per_instrument.partially_sensitive: negative_arm_clean(I) AND one_mutation_ok AND (EXISTS t: detect(I,t)) AND (EXISTS t: NOT detect(I,t))
verdict_per_instrument.insensitive: negative_arm_clean(I) AND one_mutation_ok AND NOT detect(I,t) for ALL t IN {T2,T3,T4,T5}
verdict_per_instrument.infrastructure_stop: instrument I could not be executed against the scratch copy at all. Recorded per AGENTS.md core rule 5; asserts NOTHING about sensitivity in either direction.

pass_fail_predicate.no_aggregate_verdict: There is no single batch-level pass. Four instrument rows are reported. Merging them would hide exactly the distinction this control exists to draw.
pass_fail_predicate.consequence_clause_from_the_source_contr: For any instrument whose row is `insensitive` or `partially_sensitive`, BATCH-2cca27's clause applies in its own words: 'If it does not, the procedure is broken and the verdict must be invalid, not passed.' Concretely: a future receipt-integrity `pass` produced by that instrument may not be read as evidence of intact custody at the loci where the instrument failed to detect a planted defect. This lane does NOT retroactively invalidate any committed verdict; it records what a later Coordinator must weigh.
pass_fail_predicate.predicate_is_frozen: This predicate may not be relaxed, widened, or re-scored after an outcome is observed. If the executor believes a cell is misclassified by the formula, it records the cell verbatim under defect_surfaced_otherwise (below) and leaves the formula's answer standing. Changing it requires a versioned protocol_amendment recorded before re-scoring.
pass_fail_predicate.defect_surfaced_otherwise: REQUIRED on every cell where detect(I,t) is false. Records verbatim whether the instrument surfaced the defect through some OTHER channel -- a different step or locus, an exception, a message omitting one of the two values -- with the raw output. This widens the RECORDING without weakening the predicate, so a predicate-strictness question and an instrument-blindness question stay distinguishable instead of being resolved by whoever writes the summary.

every command issued, with CAPTURED stdout, stderr, returncode and elapsed seconds

limitations, including the two named in scope_and_transfer below

deliberately_not_done, for anything in this contract not performed

required_artifacts.on_refusal_still_write_both: If the assigned session cannot honour the requested policy, or the task must stop early, it STILL writes start.json and report.json at their declared paths -- report.json with verdict `incomplete` or `refused`, listing exactly which cells ran. This is not a formality: the snapshot archive binds these paths, and a session that returns nothing leaves an archive that cannot bind. TASK-20260905-5681fc did this correctly under BATCH-2cca27 and its refusal is durable because of it.

stopping_rule: Run T1 for an instrument before planting any mutation for it. If negative_arm_clean(I) is false, STOP that instrument's sensitivity trials, record its row as `invalid` or `infrastructure_stop` with the captured evidence, and move to the next instrument.
Run T2, T3, T4, T5 in order, each on a FRESH trial directory copied from the named commits. Never reuse a trial directory.

Stop when all 20 cells are recorded, or when the advisory wall-clock estimate is reached -- in which case stop starting new cells, finish the in-flight cell, and write report.json with verdict `incomplete` naming exactly which cells ran. Do not wait to be interrupted.
NEVER repeat a cell to obtain a different outcome. A cell's first recorded outcome is its outcome. A second run of the same cell is a separate, disclosed row with its own reason for existing.

If a mutation cannot be applied as declared (the field is absent, or the from_value does not match), STOP that trial, record the mismatch with both values, and mark the trial `invalid`. Do not substitute another field or another value: the mutation set is frozen.
prohibitions: No write of any kind inside the repository except the declared artifact paths under this task's own directory. The mutated copy NEVER exists inside the checkout.
No modification of any committed byte, any receipt, any queue, any ledger record, or any archive -- in this goal or any other.
No solver execution, no benchmark, no SAT call, no research run. maximum_runs is 0.
No network request, no installation, no package fetch, no Bedrock provider, endpoint, or model identifier (AGENTS.md core rule 16).
No scientific claim, no hypothesis status change, no goal status change, no evidence record, no knowledge promotion, no completion-criterion satisfaction.
No unblocking of TASK-20260905-e2c12f or TASK-20260905-86ea49, which stay blocked per DEC-20260905-36847f and DEC-20260905-6e8621.

No repair of the two defects DEC-20260905-6e8621 named for supersession -- the by_severity low/informational miscount in the bound report bytes, and research_goal.updated_at still reading 2026-09-05. They are named, carried forward, and NOT this lane's work. Editing either in place would repeat the dd8bb7d6f error.
No editing of BATCH-008925's or BATCH-2cca27's directories, lanes, claims, or records.
Workers never commit. Every commit in this lane is made by a Coordinator archival task.

Nothing else.

Not to mutation classes other than a declared digest value and a declared parent value -- in particular NOT to a mutated commit_sha, a mutated path SET, a removed entry, an added entry, or a mutated record_ids list. A procedure sensitive to the two tested classes may be blind to any of those.

Not to the exact unpreserved instrument the delivered BATCH-008925 review executed. Instrument A is the program's archive gate and instrument B is a re-implementation of the specification; neither is that script, and no result here licenses a statement about its sensitivity.
Not to any mathematical, cryptanalytic, or complexity claim. There is none here to transfer.
declared_limitations_that_must_appear_in: Instrument B is written by the same agent that plants the mutations. Pre-registration of its sha256 in start.json before the first mutation, and the prohibition on trial-specific logic, bound this but do not eliminate it. Instrument A does not carry this limitation, which is one reason it is primary.

The four true (from-)values are declared in this contract. The reviewer's blind re-derivation is blind from the PRODUCER's artifacts, not from the Coordinator's declaration, so it localises a disagreement to the producer's implementation and cannot independently discover an error in this contract's own declared values.
